heading: LEARN MORE AND SEE WHERE TO START.
GOOGLE SAYS AI CHATBOTS ARE HURTING ITS BOTTOM LINE (2 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Google's AI search features are putting pressure on its core advertising business. Search volume growth slowed from 19% in Q1 to 12% in Q3 while search revenue remained flat. Google says AI Mode queries generate less ad revenue and plans to expand ads across AI Overviews and AI Mode to offset the impact. As more users turn to chatbots for answers, Google faces a challenge in maintaining ad revenue while investing in increasingly costly AI features.

heading: CAN ADVERTISING FUND FREE AI? EVIDENCE FROM CHATGPT'S INTERNATIONAL ADVERTISING ROLLOUT (2 MINUTE READ)
blurb: ChatGPT's current advertising model cannot yet fund free access because its ads deliver less value to advertisers than established search channels. Ads reduced organic referral traffic by 6% to 8%, but conversion rates remained unchanged at 2.21%. Paid ChatGPT visitors generated $0.89 in revenue per session compared with $2.45 for Google Search and converted at less than a third of the rate. ChatGPT would need to lower ad prices substantially to compete with Google and make its free tier financially sustainable.

heading: SUBSTACK IS A $0 CHEAT CODE FOR YOUR BRAND (3 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Substack can send a newsletter roughly 50X more subscribers than Google, since every signup surfaces a few newsletters the writer recommends. Companies are tapping that loop with behind-the-scenes posts from the people building the product. PostHog recommends 10 engineering newsletters that all recommend it back, while Ramp gets a recommendation from TBPN's Substack as part of its sponsorship. Substack's audience stats rank which newsletters already share a brand's readers, pointing to the best swap partners.

heading: ALGOS WIKI (WEBSITE)
blurb: Algos.wiki is an unofficial, AI-powered encyclopedia of Instagram's algorithm that organizes information from platform announcements and leadership interviews into searchable topics. Use it to research how content is ranked and recommended, including how posting times and shares affect reach. It also tracks algorithm updates and links to supporting sources.

heading: 6 APP GROWTH ANNUAL WORKSHOPS YOU CAN WATCH FOR FREE (+ PRESENTER SLIDES) (6 MINUTE READ)
blurb: RevenueCat has made 6 App Growth Annual workshops free to watch, with presenter slides and handouts. Sessions cover mining customer feedback to write higher-converting copy and researching users to drive organic downloads. Others show how to use competitor ads to create AI-generated creatives and automate Meta ad research and optimization with AI.

heading: REACH IS NOT PROOF (4 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Retailer-owned shopping agents have the strongest evidence of sales impact, while ChatGPT and Google have massive reach but no published purchase results. Amazon reports nearly $12B in incremental annualized sales from its assistant, while Walmart says Sparky users spend 40% more per order. Brands should make product data complete and accessible so agents can accurately evaluate and recommend their products. AI-driven discovery is already happening, but sales impact remains unproven across most categories.

heading: WHEN BUNDLING HURTS THE BOTTOM LINE (6 MINUTE READ)
blurb: When demand far outstrips inventory, selling items separately beats package deals and earns nearly as much as the best possible bundling mix. Bundling works with ample stock because it averages out how much each buyer values each item, widening the customer base. Under scarcity, that same averaging caps how high a bundle can be priced, while separate prices capture each item's top bidders. Selling separately can start to win once available inventory falls below about 30-60% of potential customers.

heading: CREATOR SPONSORSHIP PRICES ARE NEGOTIATED UPWARD FROM A LOW FIRST OFFER, DATA SHOWS (5 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Creator sponsorship deals often close well above a brand's first offer, which averaged just 27% of the creator's quoted price across 124 negotiations. Creators can negotiate higher rates by adjusting deliverables rather than cutting prices and using average views and CPMs to justify fees. Paid usage adds 30-40% to the rate. Longer-term partnerships also provide more predictable income while helping creators reduce reliance on one-off sponsorships.

heading: ‘THE CONTENT CREATOR ELECTION': DIGITAL STREAMERS AND TV NETWORKS FACE OFF FOR MIDTERMS COVERAGE (5 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Former TV journalists are launching independent election-night livestreams on YouTube and Substack, challenging traditional networks as creator-led news gains traction.

heading: WHAT REDDIT'S Q3 EARNINGS MEAN FOR MARKETERS AMID MAJOR TRAFFIC SHIFT (3 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Reddit's referral traffic is falling by over 1M visits per week as Google's AI Overviews reduce clicks to the platform.

heading: HOW I GET 1M VIEWS/WEEK FOR MY STARTUP (5 MINUTE READ)
blurb: A founder shares his Reddit growth strategy, from content creation to building trust without hard-selling.

heading: TRY IT FREE FOR 14 DAYS.
AI TRAFFIC DRIVES 83% MORE REVENUE PER VISIT (2 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Adobe found that AI-referred traffic generated 83% more revenue per visit and converted 90% better than non-AI traffic in September. AI visitors also spent 73% more time on site and added products to carts 53% more often. However, the average retail homepage scored just 63% on Adobe's AI readability measure. Product specifications, setup guides, and customer service pages were easier for AI to understand.

heading: COMPANIES MAY NEED TO RESTRICT AI USE TO MANAGE COSTS (3 MINUTE READ)
blurb: OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, and Meta are spending billions on AI development but struggling to turn their investments into profits. OpenAI reported more than $20B in operating losses in the first half of 2026, while Anthropic's infrastructure costs have surged 329% year over year. xAI has already restricted Grok access because of high operating costs. AI companies may introduce tighter usage limits to control spending as pressure to deliver returns grows.

heading: LET'S GET THE FIRST 100 USERS FOR A STARTUP (4 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Many of the best early-user channels work because they're too small for bigger companies to chase. Smaller podcasts are often short on guests and open to founders who demo the product on air. Newsletters under 10K subscribers cost a few hundred dollars to sponsor and often beat larger ones on ROI. Buying a tiny app with an overlapping audience for $1K to $10K gives a ready base of users to redirect.

heading: FLIGHTCAST (TOOL)
blurb: Flightcast lets creators automatically distribute their existing YouTube video catalogs to Spotify for $100/month. Creators can connect their YouTube accounts and transfer individual videos, playlists, or entire catalogs, with future uploads syndicated automatically. Flightcast also adapts titles, descriptions, and chapters for Spotify.

heading: WHY PR IS THE NEW SEO (THANKS TO AI) (40 MINUTE PODCAST)
blurb: AI is bringing SEO and PR closer together as brands compete for visibility beyond website clicks. Amanda Milligan from Semrush explains why earned media and third-party mentions influence AI visibility. She also shares how Semrush builds its B2B YouTube strategy by balancing search-driven videos with content designed for YouTube's recommendation algorithm.

heading: HOW TEXT OVERLAYS IN SOCIAL MEDIA IMAGES AFFECT ENGAGEMENT (2 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Large or centered text overlays lower engagement when the image underneath is dynamic. A busy image already draws the eye, so big central text creates a competing focal point that makes the post look disorganized. Static images can carry larger, centered text, which guides attention instead of fighting for it.

heading: AUDIENCE ANALYSIS FOR CRM AND EMAIL: HOW TO UNDERSTAND PEOPLE WELL ENOUGH TO SEND THE RIGHT MESSAGE AT THE RIGHT TIME (8 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Effective CRM marketing starts with understanding what people need when you contact them, not just who they are or what triggered an email. Track opt-in type and relationship stage in your CRM to distinguish intentional subscribers from people who signed up for a download or were added to a list. Analyze customer motivations and emotions around key triggers, collect the language they use to describe their needs, and review their email history to spot irrelevant or repetitive messages. Turn these insights into CRM properties and workflow rules that inform messaging at every stage of the relationship. Measure success through engagement by opt-in type, conversions by intent level, and fewer emails per conversion.

heading: WHEN 10.3% IS BETTER THAN 10% (3 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Precise figures make a feature count more in purchase decisions than rounded ones, but only for features where lower is better, like weight or price.

heading: YOUR AI SEARCH NUMBERS FEEL GOOD. THEY MIGHT BE CHANCE. (6 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Small samples carry wide ranges, so a month-to-month gain may be chance rather than the result of new content.

heading: THE 25 BEST AEO/GEO EXPERTS TO FOLLOW IN 2026 (20 MINUTE READ)
blurb: 25 people who are publishing the most original research on AI search.

heading: CHATGPT HAS HIT ROUGHLY 20% OF GOOGLE SEARCH VOLUME (1 MINUTE READ)
blurb: OpenAI says ChatGPT search volume has reached roughly 20% of Google Search's volume, making it Google's biggest search competitor yet. The estimate counts prompts that trigger a web search and may not be directly comparable to Google's search figures. ChatGPT's growth is driving Google to expand AI features in Search. OpenAI also says users value ChatGPT's personalization and is considering expanding its use of ads.

heading: IS B2B SAAS STILL BLOGGING? (7 MINUTE READ)
blurb: An analysis of blog posts from 219 mid-market B2B SaaS companies found total publishing volume across 187 companies increased 37% YoY and 151% since ChatGPT launched. Half of companies published more posts this year while median output rose from 42 to 62 posts annually. 52% of posts were how-tos, explainers, or comparisons. Only 2.4% contained original research or perspectives. Posts were also 55% longer, and posts per author increased 73%.

heading: CREATED A CONTENT COLLAB FORMULA TO DRIVE REVENUE & NEWSLETTER SIGNUPS (2 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Content partnerships can drive newsletter growth without paid placements. Start by identifying newsletters with overlapping audiences and pitch data-backed research that fits their readers. Build the relationship before asking for promotional CTAs. Then actively promote each collaboration to make it worthwhile for both sides. One company attributes 60-70% of new newsletter signups to 3 recommendation engines that continue driving subscribers months after the original collaborations.

heading: HE'S DONE 852 B2B VIDEO ADS, HERE'S WHAT THE TOP 1% HAVE IN COMMON (4 MINUTE READ)
blurb: The strongest B2B video ads are built for a viewer who will probably skip them. The brand name lands in the first 5 seconds, and the product appears one feature at a time as a simple input and output. Hooks name a specific, emotional problem, and benefits become a moment the viewer can picture instead of a promise of saved time. Each cut is made for its specific channel, with an exaggerated prop like a dusty onboarding binder to make it more memorable.

heading: HTML VS. XML SITEMAPS FOR ECOMMERCE (2 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Ecommerce sites should use both XML and HTML sitemaps to improve page discovery, crawling, and indexing. XML sitemaps automatically list every URL intended for indexing, while HTML sitemaps provide users and search engines with links to important categories, subcategories, and site pages. HTML sitemaps can also strengthen internal linking and help reduce the number of pages that Google crawls but does not index. Neither replaces a well-organized site hierarchy or strong internal linking, but HTML sitemaps can serve as a temporary solution during site restructures.

heading: HOW TO USE GOOGLE ANALYTICS FOR SOCIAL MEDIA (GA4 SETUP + REPORTS) (11 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Use GA4 to measure what happens after someone clicks a social media link by tracking website traffic, engagement, conversions, and revenue. Start by setting up key events for actions like form submissions, purchases, and signups, then add UTM parameters to every social link to identify the platform, campaign, and specific post generating traffic. Use GA4's Traffic Acquisition, User Acquisition, Landing Page, and Attribution reports to compare platform performance, evaluate landing pages, and understand how social contributes to conversions across the customer journey. Build a Looker Studio dashboard to track these metrics over time and report social media's contribution to leads and revenue.

heading: WHICH TYPES OF MENTIONS CORRELATE THE STRONGEST WITH AI VISIBILITY? (9 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Off-site brand mentions correlate with visibility in ChatGPT, AI Mode, and AI Overviews. Reddit mentions had the strongest correlation (0.75), ahead of general web mentions (0.70) and press coverage (0.67). Brands with 10X more Reddit mentions typically received 5.5X more AI mentions, while 10X more webpage mentions correlated with 3.7X more. These are correlations, not proof that mentions cause AI visibility.

heading: AI AGENT MESSAGING: WHAT 1,014 SOFTWARE BUYERS WANT (5 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Describing an AI product as a team of specialized agents generates more purchase interest than describing it as a single agent. A survey of 1,014 software buyers found that team framing increased purchase intent by 6.3 percentage points compared to single-agent framing. However, calling a product an agent alone did not increase purchase interest and slightly reduced it. Buyers also perceived products described as multiple agents as harder to use, while perceptions of helpfulness and trustworthiness remained largely unchanged. The findings suggest that breaking a product into distinct functions can increase its perceived value through a psychological phenomenon known as the unpacking effect.

heading: THE GROWTH PLAYBOOK EVERYONE KEEPS USING (9 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Growth teams keep recycling the same tactics, like price increases, upmarket moves, and big launches. Most have worked at some point, which is why they return every few years under new names. The trouble is that they're often used to avoid fixing what's broken in the product or the company. Tactics are easy to assign owners and report progress on, while core problems don't fit a quarterly roadmap. Strong growth leaders stand out by knowing which problems are worth solving, then picking tactics that fit.

heading: WE ARE TESTING AD PLACEMENTS IN REDDIT SEARCH PAGES (1 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Half of Reddit users say the platform helps them discover something new, which makes its search pages a high-intent spot for ads.

heading: PERSONALITY IS THE NEW FUEL FOR MARKETING (4 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Personality-led brands codify the rhythms of how they talk, so they stay recognizable in a social reply or a Super Bowl ad.

heading: CANVA CUT 1,271 ROLES WITHOUT BLAMING AI. CHATGPT IS STILL EATING ITS FREE TIER (6 MINUTE READ)
blurb: Canva is betting on brand management as AI makes design creation easier and cheaper.
